review_evidence: README states the repository formalizes the bread-and-butter of matroid theory and enumerates isomorphism, circuits, rank, minors, flats, modularity, representability, connectivity, intersection, uniform matroids and excluded-minor results.

Representative source includes transversal_exists_iff, unif_is_transversal, quotient/rank lemmas and extensive definitions/constructions; this is unambiguously high-value mathematical formalization prior art.
summary: Reviewed Matroid and retain its large formalization of matroid theory.

review_evidence: Surveyed the checkout root (`find . -maxdepth 1`): source subdirectories are `Matroid`, `notes`, `tests`, `WIP`, `InfiniteModular`, `scripts`; build config is `lakefile.toml` (not `.lean`), out of this unit's 46-file review scope.

Ran a Lean declaration-marker grep (theorem|lemma|def |structure|inductive|class |instance|abbrev|macro|elab|syntax|axiom) across all 46 files: scores ranged from 0 to 188, with only two files scoring below 9: `Matroid/Exercises/HamiltonianCycle/Connected.lean` (0 hits, 52 bytes) and `Matroid.lean` (1 hit, 9604 bytes).

Read `Matroid/Exercises/HamiltonianCycle/Connected.lean` in full (52 bytes): consists of exactly `module` + one `public import Matroid.Graph.Connected.Basic` line -- a trivial pure import aggregator, zero declarations.

Read `Matroid.lean` in full (9604 bytes): a root-level `module` + ~230-line `public import` list over the entire `Matroid` namespace tree (Axioms, Connectivity, Extension, Graph, Representation, Uniform, etc.), no declarations of its own. Its single grep hit (line 147, `public import Matroid.Graph.Relabel`) was checked with `grep -noE` and is a false positive: the substring `elab` inside `Relabel`, not the `elab` keyword. Confirmed FILTER-007 pure import aggregator (many import targets, e.g. Matroid.Axioms.Circuit, Matroid.BaseExchange, are pre-existing files outside this unit's 46-file diff); retained, no exclusion rule needed, consistent with this session's cross-source precedent for such root navigation files (mattrobball__BridgelandStability.lean, PierreSenellart__provenance-lean's Provenance.lean).

Read the lowest-scoring genuine-content file, `Matroid/Transport.lean` (9 hits, 3362 bytes), in full: defines canonical-transport equivalences under matroid isomorphism (`supportedSetEquiv`, `Iso.elementDomain`, `Iso.groundSetEquiv`, etc.) with full proofs -- genuine.

Read the head of the largest/highest-hit file, `Matroid/ForMathlib/Tactic/IRw.lean` (188 hits, 114415 bytes): a custom `irw` (isomorphism-rewriting) tactic implementation with `register_grind_attr`, attribute registries (`@[irw_system]`, `@[irw_domain]`, `@[irw_support]`, `@[irw_naturality]`, `@[irw_equiv]`), and an extensive doc comment describing the tactic's design -- genuine project-owned proof-automation infrastructure, not build/CI tooling.

Spot-checked the two similarly-named `Matroid/Extremal/Covers.lean` (113 hits, 70832 bytes) and `Matroid/Extremal/Covers_.lean` (85 hits, 56712 bytes) via `head`: distinct content (different lemma/theorem names and statements), not a duplicate pair -- both genuine, independent developments.

No file matched a known exclusion pattern from this session's precedents (Lake/CI build tooling, Verso-generated narrative manual, generated benchmark-data dump with no statement content, exact duplicate) beyond the two pure-import files already retained under FILTER-007.
